messages:
emily-sales: FYI ACME legal looped in. They want p95=120ms / p99=220ms at sustained 60 QPS. Can eng confirm this on Dedicated (g5x-large profile)? Asking for an SLA clause.
alex-kim: Short answer: difficult but maybe. p95 120ms looks doable with microbatch=1 + tuned kernel (A-fast) + warm KV cache. p99 220ms depends on tail behavior from KV cold misses + microbatching spikes. Need concrete perf numbers and root-cause for recent p99 spikes.
maria-gonzalez: Pasted quick 48h profiling after commit abc123 (high-level):
```
Before abc123 (sampled 500k tokens): p50=18ms p95=110ms p99=190ms p999=420ms | KV hit=86% | kernel=A
After abc123 (500k tokens): p50=20ms p95=130ms p99=310ms p999=760ms | KV hit=68% | kernel=A
Note: single-token paths dominate; seq len 32 typical. Observed more KV_CACHE: MISS at tail.
```
jordan: I dug into logs — the KV pruning tweak in abc123 reduced cache residency for low-weight prefixes. When a request hits a miss we rebuild KV chain which adds ~120-400ms on tail. Sample log:
```
[2026-03-17T09:12:04Z] req=0x7f KV_CACHE: MISS prefix=~"Hello" rebuild_time=0.135s
```
sam-product: Sales needs a concrete ask. If engineering can't promise 120/220 we should propose alternatives to ACME: higher p95, longer warmup, or a staged SLA (canary -> ramp). What are the tradeoffs to present?
lee-wang: Options we can offer:
- Hot-KV pool pinned to customer (reduces misses, increases cost)
- Fallback model-variant (small-quant) with faster kernels and lower quality
- Per-route microbatch policy: microbatch=1 under 80 QPS, dynamic batching above that
Config snippet example (per-route):
```
route("/v1/gen").microbatching = {min=1, max=4, latencyTargetMs=120}
route("/v1/gen").kvPolicy = "hot-pinned"
```
alex-kim: Measured tradeoffs: with small-quant fallback (auto-fallback when latency > threshold): p95~130ms p99~200ms, but eval quality drops ~1.2 bleu-ish points on our internal metric. Dynamic microbatching to increase throughput (max=4) can improve overall QPS by ~30%, but increases median/p95 by ~10-20ms depending on seq distribution.
maria-gonzalez: Proposal to meet Sales/Customer halfway: 1) dedicated hot-KV for ACME, 2) kernel pin to A-fast for their model, 3) per-route microbatch policy (min=1, dynamic up to 3), 4) canary 2 weeks. I ran a short sim combining hot-KV + fallback and got:
```
sim (hot-kv + small-fallback): p50=22ms p95=125ms p99=215ms KV_hit~95%
```
This looks within range of what Sales asked, but still depends on long-term KV working set stability. We also need a kernel tweak for longer seqs to avoid p999 spikes.
emily-sales: ACME will push back on anything that increases p99 >220ms. Can we offer an SLA with a small buffer and a mitigation plan (credits + escalation) instead of 100% guarantee? They prefer a commitment in contract.
alex-kim: We can commit to SLA if Product & Sales accept: - Dedicated hot-KV (ops cost), - Pin kernel variant A-fast for that model, - Per-route microbatch policy, - 2-week canary + 1-month probation for telemetry, - fallback model as safe guard. Also require a rollback plan and runbook for KV warm-up. Action: I will run a full perf job (1M token sample) and post final numbers by EOD.
perf-bot: Perf job started: run_id=r-20260317-42; profile_target=1,000,000 tokens; kernels=[A-fast, small-quant]; kv_mode=hot-pinned; ETA=6h
maria-gonzalez: Created infra ticket INF-4521 for hot-KV provisioning + ops playbook. Also filed RUNTIME-3187 for kernel re-tune. I'll attach sim logs when perf job finishes.
emily-sales: Thanks all. I'll draft the SLA wording: propose p95=125ms / p99=215ms with a clause: if p99>220ms for >4 hours/month then 2% service credit. Also propose canary and monthly review for 3 months. I'll share draft with @sam-product and legal.
alex-kim: Sounds good. On my side: running perf collect + small ablation test for microbatch thresholds. Will ping thread with numbers. If results are outside target, we either increase hot-kv capacity or push fallback threshold lower.
emily-sales: :+1: Action items: (1) alex run perf & post results (EOD) (2) infra ticket INF-4521 (maria) (3) SLA draft (emily/sam) (4) runbook + rollback (ops). Thanks everyone.
